# COR081 `magic-io-unit`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="info" text="opt-in" />

An I/O statement uses a literal unit number.

## Why

Literal unit numbers collide: a library and the program both opening unit 10 silently share (or
close) one file, and units 5 and 6 are only conventionally the terminal. Open files with
`newunit=` and use `input_unit`/`output_unit`/`error_unit` from `iso_fortran_env`.

## Reported

```fortran
open(10, file='mesh.dat')
read(10, *) n
```

## Preferred

```fortran
open(newunit=u, file='mesh.dat')
read(u, *) n
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR081] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR081` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `C032` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
